cases.answer: The TyG/CAD-RADS study defined MACE as a composite of myocardial infarction, all-cause mortality and stroke. Follow-up was long: median 50.4 months (IQR 39.4–55.1), counted from the coronary CTA date to MACE or the follow-up deadline. 212 patients (6.0%) had MACE. Gao's CCTA nomogram study defined MACE as cardiac death including fatal MI, non-fatal MI, coronary revascularization for unstable angina, and rehospitalization for unstable angina. Follow-up there was 1 year from the first CCTA, ending at the first event or the study termination date (December 31, 2023), with monthly assessments. 46 of 280 patients (16.43%) had MACE. In Gao's cohort, 30 of the 46 events (65.22%) were rehospitalization for unstable angina. Gao's definition has no stroke or all-cause death component, and TyG's has no revascularization or rehospitalization component.

cases.answer: The primary efficacy endpoint was freedom from any documented episode of AF lasting longer than 30 s after the 3-month blanking period, occurring after a single ablation procedure, with or without antiarrhythmic drugs. At 12 months in the mITT population (n = 357), the estimated probability of treatment success was 88% for the tailored (AI-guided spatio-temporal dispersion plus PVI) arm and 70% for the anatomical (PVI-only) arm (HR 0.3; 95% CI 0.21–0.57; log-rank P < 0.0001), so the trial met the endpoint. Counts: tailored arm 158 achieved the endpoint, 22 did not and 7 had no follow-up beyond blanking; anatomical arm 124 achieved it, 53 did not and 6 had no follow-up.

cases.answer: Added drug: the Cameroon trial added spironolactone, 25 mg daily, on top of ongoing therapy in T2DM patients with resistant hypertension, compared with an alternative antihypertensive regimen. EMPEROR-Preserved added empagliflozin 10 mg to usual therapy in HFpEF patients, compared with placebo, and the analysis was by hypertension category (including resistant HTN). Follow-up: the Cameroon trial was 4 weeks, with visits at start, 2 and 4 weeks. EMPEROR-Preserved reported SBP effects over 172 weeks. BP change: in Cameroon, office SBP fell 33 vs 14 mmHg and DBP 14 vs 5 mmHg (spironolactone vs alternative; p = 0.024 and p = 0.006). In EMPEROR-Preserved resHTN, the empagliflozin vs placebo SBP difference was only 2.4–3.3 mmHg at Weeks 4–32 (P = .001–.009), and values were similar from Weeks 52–172 (P = .26–.74).
